suggestions.rationale: Upper-eyelid ptosis can mechanically obstruct the superior visual field and produce functionally significant visual impairment. Evidence-based eyelid-surgery guidance specifically addresses upper visual-field impairment related to ptosis and emphasizes documentation of the underlying cause and functional deficit. This supports a ptosis-to-visual-impairment pathway only when formal or clinically appropriate testing demonstrates a field deficit attributable to the drooping eyelid; ptosis without objective functional obstruction should not be treated as visual impairment by default.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Documented upper-eyelid ptosis → mechanical obstruction of the superior visual axis/field when sufficiently severe → objectively demonstrated visual-field impairment attributable to the eyelid position.
developmentQuestions: Is ptosis objectively documented, including laterality, severity, margin-reflex distance, levator function, and suspected cause where available?
Does formal visual-field testing or another accepted functional assessment show a superior-field deficit that corresponds to the ptotic eyelid?
Does manual eyelid elevation or taping improve the visual field when such testing is clinically appropriate?
Are visual acuity and other ocular findings consistent with a mechanical field obstruction rather than a separate retinal, optic-nerve, corneal, lenticular, or neurologic cause?
Did ptosis repair improve the documented functional deficit if surgery occurred?
issuesToResolve: Ptosis can be cosmetically apparent without producing a qualifying functional visual deficit; objective field impairment and attribution to eyelid position are required.
The cause of ptosis and other ocular or neurologic causes of visual impairment should be evaluated separately rather than conflated with mechanical superior-field obstruction.

evidenceGaps: Ophthalmology or oculoplastic examination documenting ptosis severity and laterality
Objective visual-field or other accepted functional testing showing impairment attributable to eyelid position
Taped/elevated-lid comparison or postoperative functional response when available
Assessment of competing ocular and neurologic causes of the visual deficit
Clinician opinion linking the documented functional impairment to the individual ptosis

sourceReferences.citation: Kim KK et al. American Society of Plastic Surgeons Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline: Eyelid Surgery for Upper Visual Field Improvement. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2022;150(2):419e-434e. PMID 35895522
sourceReferences.note: Evidence-based guideline addresses upper visual-field impairment related to eyelid ptosis and dermatochalasis and emphasizes documentation of the cause of visual-field impairment. Supports an objective function-limited ptosis pathway, while the guideline notes limitations in the methodological quality of much of the surgical literature.
